rationale: `overrides` is the one type CSS was emitting nothing for and the language DOES have. Measured over the whole admitted corpus (1,114 files, 61 repos; validation/m14/census/css-overrides-split.ts): 146 adjacent same-name second declarations of a `@keyframes` in one file, of which 142 are a VENDOR-PREFIXED PAIR and 4 are genuine same-keyword redefinitions (hasura-engine/.../GraphiQL.css `@keyframes rotation` at L1534 and L2214, plus `v-modal-in`, `v-modal-out` and `progress` in vue-element-admin). So the type is a GAP on 4 occurrences and a FABRICATION on the other 142, and one fixture has to pin both halves or it pins neither: `fade` is declared twice with the same keyword and must produce an `overrides` edge naming the block it kills, `slide` is declared under two different keywords and must produce NONE. A lane that got this wrong in the first direction would add 142 fabricated edges to a corpus of 1,114 files; in the second it would ship the type with no evidence. The `@property` pair is the third case: the Properties & Values API's re-registration rule, 0 corpus occurrences, pinned here because a measured zero is a fact about the corpus and not about the construct — the same standing answer this lane gave `@counter-style`/`@custom-media`/`@font-feature-values`. The `overrides` edge's two ends are the same string by construction (the lane publishes one symbol per name, and a selector/name is an identity rather than a per-occurrence row), so the payload is the LINE PAIR: `line_number` is the superseding declaration and `supersedesLine` is the one it kills. That is why the pins below assert `supersedesLine` and not just the type.
_targetSpelling: CSS-D15: a target that names a declaration THIS file publishes is spelled `<file-scope>::<name>`, where the scope is the file's project-relative path without its extension. The bare spelling stays for a target this file does not declare (a cross-file or external reference) and for `imports`, whose target is another file's module name.
